controls.label: Shape
controls.notes: The shared neutral gray marks unavailable surface imagery over the released MPCD shape reconstructed from ground-based VLT/SPHERE images. The two lobes and narrow neck are source geometry. This view has no photographic texture and does not represent albedo, color or composition. Lighting uses the observed pole with an arbitrary display phase. Neutral gray (#808080 sRGB) is a shared display convention, not measured surface color or albedo.

controls.label: SPHERE photograph
controls.notes: 55 deconvolved VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL frames, 10 nights from 2017-07-14 to 2019-01-14, cast onto the ADAM reconstruction from the same survey. The survey’s rotation record describes that frame, so the photograph rides it rather than the model the Shape view uses. Pointing and orientation are computed from that record, JPL Horizons geometry and each frame’s header, at the midpoint of its exposure; the disc centre is fitted to the limb of the mesh. With these cameras the mesh reproduces Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.37. Grayscale is photographed illumination and matched relative frame brightness, each apparition placed through the surface it shares with another. The deconvolution carries no radiometric calibration, so this is not measured albedo or colour. The grid marks surface that was unphotographed, too grazing, or rejected.
